facts.statement: Ceramornis is a genus of ornithuran dinosaurs that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Ceramornis is a genus of ornithuran dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Ceramornis lived in the Maastrichtian stage, shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: It lived shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event in the Maastrichtian, some Paleogene million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Ceramornis were discovered at the Lull 2 site in the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: Its remains were found in the Lull 2 location, a Lance Formation site in Niobrara County, Wyoming.

facts.statement: The only known species, Ceramornis major, is represented solely by a proximal fragment of a coracoid bone.
facts.quote: A single species is known, Ceramornis major, and even that only from a proximal piece of coracoid.

facts.statement: The single known specimen, UCMP V53957, was collected by a University of California team in 1958.
facts.quote: This is specimen UCMP V53957, which was collected by a University of California team in 1958.

facts.statement: Ceramornis is classified within the family Cimolopterygidae alongside the genera Cimolopteryx and Lamarqueavis.
facts.quote: Ceramornis has been placed in the family Cimolopterygidae together with Cimolopteryx and Lamarqueavis.

facts.statement: The family Cimolopterygidae has occasionally been assigned to the modern bird order Charadriiformes based on coracoid analysis.
facts.quote: Cimolopterygidae has sometimes been placed in the modern bird order Charadriiformes, based on quantitative analysis of its coracoid and comparison with other modern bird samples.

facts.statement: There is uncertainty regarding the taxonomic placement of Ceramornis due to insufficient fossil material for comprehensive cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: However, there remains some uncertainty about the taxonomic position, as there is insufficient fossil material to be assessed by wide-scale cladistic analysis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the bird order Charadriiformes was already distinct during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: It is not certain that Charadriiformes was already distinct by the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Ceramornis lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
